gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow's X-Boost runs high-watt loads by lowering the output voltage, that EcoFlow's manual says it is 'more suitable for heating devices', and that it is 'unavailable when the power station is connected to an AC power source' (charging or bypass). So when a DELTA 3 Plus sits on wall power as a 10 ms UPS, its ceiling is the rated 1,800 W, not the 2,600 W X-Boost figure.
standout_why: I compared against solarkontor.de (rank 1), explorersweb.com DELTA Max review (rank 4) and EcoFlow's own US store copy. Solarkontor's whole account of X-Boost is that 'the capacity can be temporarily doubled to power devices with high inrush currents'. That is the opposite of what the maker's manual says, because X-Boost lowers voltage and is aimed at heating loads. Solarkontor gives no switchover time and says nothing about X-Boost turning off while charging. Explorersweb mentions neither X-Boost nor UPS. EcoFlow's US store copy lists 'refrigerators, washers, circular saws' and 'air conditioner' as X-Boost loads, while its manual points to heating devices. Trailandkale (404) and tech.yahoo.com (403) would not open, and I did not open the techradar tag page, REI or the two notebookcheck news posts.
decides: Size the EcoFlow to its rated watts, not its X-Boost watts. That matters most for motor loads such as fridges, sump pumps and AC, and for any setup where the unit stays plugged in as a UPS, because X-Boost turns off then. A shopper who needs about 2,000 W of non-heating load while it acts as a 10 ms UPS should skip the 1,800 W DELTA 3 Plus and DELTA 3 Classic and go to the 3,000 W DELTA 3 Max Plus or the 3,600 W DELTA 3 Ultra.

findings.label: X-Boost: which loads it suits
findings.value: 'X-Boost is more suitable for heating devices, such as an electric blanket, a water heater, or a heat pump. X-Boost does not support devices with voltage protection (such as precise instruments). If such devices are connected, they may stop working due to low voltage.'
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus User Manual, page 20 (ManualsLib mirror)
findings.note: Quoted from the manual page. EcoFlow's own copy is at ecoflow-service-us-prod.oss-us-west-1.aliyuncs.com/cms/manual/1753868222389/EcoFlow%20DELTA%203%20Plus_User%20Manual.pdf. I downloaded it but could not extract its text, so the quotes come from the ManualsLib mirror of the same manual.

findings.label: X-Boost turns off on AC input
findings.value: 'X-Boost is unavailable when the power station is connected to an AC power source (e.g. The power station is charging or in [bypass] mode).' Bypass mode starts automatically when the unit charges and discharges through AC at the same time.
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus User Manual, page 20 (ManualsLib mirror)
findings.note: The word 'bypass' is cut off in the page text. The manual's own footnote on the same page defines bypass mode. This is the mechanism: UPS use is AC-in plus AC-out, which is bypass mode, so X-Boost is off.

findings.label: AC output at 120 V, rated and with X-Boost
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus User Manual, page 20 (ManualsLib mirror)
findings.note: From the manual's 'Reference: Power with X-Boost Feature' table, 120 V row. On AC input (UPS or bypass) only the 1,800 W applies.

findings.label: UPS transfer time
findings.value: 10 ms ('acts as a standby UPS with a transfer time of 10 ms')
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus User Manual, page 20 (ManualsLib mirror)
findings.note: The manual calls it a standby (offline) UPS, not online double-conversion.

findings.label: How X-Boost works (maker's words)
findings.value: 'intelligent voltage control that marginally reduces voltage', which lets devices run on a lower-rated inverter. It is unavailable while the unit is charging, and EcoFlow says not to connect the AC output to the grid while X-Boost is on.
findings.note: EcoFlow's example loads on this page are mostly resistive: air fryer 1,500 W, kettle 1,500 W, heater 2,200 W, hair dryer 1,600 W. The page says nothing about motors or compressors.
